# Hugh Carrow

## Overview

- **Gender:** Male  <sub>[v1 c15 P37](../source/v01-c15.md#nw-v01-c15-p0037), [v2 c19 P50](../source/v02-c19.md#nw-v02-c19-p0050), [v3 c5 P1](../source/v03-c05.md#nw-v03-c05-p0001)</sub>
- **Role:** Daily News employee; student  <sub>[v3 c5 P0](../source/v03-c05.md#nw-v03-c05-p0000), [v3 c20 P23](../source/v03-c20.md#nw-v03-c20-p0023)</sub>

## Appearance

Hugh is described as a manly, tall youth with broad shoulders and bright, direct eyes. He bears a striking resemblance to his father as a young man. In his youth, he was an open-faced and good-looking guy.

_Sources: [v2 c19 P50](../source/v02-c19.md#nw-v02-c19-p0050)_

## Personality

Hugh is popular, brave, and possesses an open and direct demeanor, though he is persistent in pursuing his desires. He holds high principles and guards his speech, thoughts, and actions carefully to remain worthy of good companionship. Driven by strong independence, he exhibits leadership abilities and takes responsibility for his actions, such as admitting fault when provoking others.

_Sources: [v1 c15 P42](../source/v01-c15.md#nw-v01-c15-p0042), [v1 c37 P40](../source/v01-c37.md#nw-v01-c37-p0040), [v2 c19 P50](../source/v02-c19.md#nw-v02-c19-p0050), [v2 c19 P51](../source/v02-c19.md#nw-v02-c19-p0051), [v3 c5 P0](../source/v03-c05.md#nw-v03-c05-p0000)_

## History

Hugh attended Brierley School, where he famously pulled Nell Harcourt's crimson plait and teased her, prompting her to break her slate over his head. Though he stepped up to take the blame for the incident, Nell refused to forgive him at the time. Over the years, he developed high principles and a strong attachment to Nell, striving to guard his behavior to be worthy of her companionship. After moving on to higher education at Wexcombe College, he led the Freshmen to victory against the Sophomores in the Arts Rush using clever tactics and was subsequently elected president of the Freshman Class. He was also invited to join the Lamba Theta fraternity ("the Lambs"), undergoing their initiation ritual with good humor. During an early spring evening, he met Nell and offered her Mayflowers, ultimately confessing his love and asking her to marry him. Upon being rejected, he was deeply heartbroken and declared that he could not be satisfied with mere friendship before taking his leave to start a new position at the Daily News.

_Sources: [v1 c15 P33](../source/v01-c15.md#nw-v01-c15-p0033), [v1 c15 P34](../source/v01-c15.md#nw-v01-c15-p0034), [v1 c15 P38](../source/v01-c15.md#nw-v01-c15-p0038), [v1 c15 P42](../source/v01-c15.md#nw-v01-c15-p0042), [v1 c15 P47](../source/v01-c15.md#nw-v01-c15-p0047), [v2 c19 P51](../source/v02-c19.md#nw-v02-c19-p0051), [v3 c5 P0](../source/v03-c05.md#nw-v03-c05-p0000), [v3 c20 P15](../source/v03-c20.md#nw-v03-c20-p0015), [v3 c20 P17](../source/v03-c20.md#nw-v03-c20-p0017), [v3 c20 P31](../source/v03-c20.md#nw-v03-c20-p0031), [v3 c20 P34](../source/v03-c20.md#nw-v03-c20-p0034), [v3 c20 P41](../source/v03-c20.md#nw-v03-c20-p0041), [v3 c20 P44](../source/v03-c20.md#nw-v03-c20-p0044)_

## Background by volume

- Attended Brierley School alongside Nell Harcourt
- Spent three years living in Alberta with his father
- Son of John Carrow

## Quotes

> Mr. Pidgeon, the blame belongs to me because I provoked her.  <sub>[v1 c15 P42](../source/v01-c15.md#nw-v01-c15-p0042)</sub>

> Nell, I’m terribly apologetic about mocking your hair. Truly I am. Please don’t stay angry forever.  <sub>[v1 c15 P49](../source/v01-c15.md#nw-v01-c15-p0049)</sub>

> Nell, do these not bring back memories of home and the picnics from our former school days?  <sub>[v3 c20 P18](../source/v03-c20.md#nw-v03-c20-p0018)</sub>

> I have to. We cannot continue in this manner anymore. Nell, my love belongs to you. You are aware of that. I—I am unable to express the extent of it. Can you give me your word that you will marry me one day?  <sub>[v3 c20 P31](../source/v03-c20.md#nw-v03-c20-p0031)</sub>

> Comrades! Nell, I am unable to be fulfilled by your friendship. It is your love that I desire—yet you inform me that it will always be out of my reach.  <sub>[v3 c20 P41](../source/v03-c20.md#nw-v03-c20-p0041)</sub>
